env.name: Environment & lighting
env.scope: Skyline, atmosphere, fog, tone mapping, bloom, SSAO, colour grade

issues.text: At the default tactical camera, Arad is still a near-perfect octagon of equal square blocks, each outlined by a bright tan walk strip. From S7 it reads as a glowing coin, and from S2 as a game board. The racetrack loop is gone, but the replacement villa quarter and the west industrial area both read from above as symmetric forked 'tridents' or feather shapes (a spine that splits into 2-3 short prongs with a single row of houses on each). That is just as procedural a tell. The NE slab quarter and west sheds are thin strings, not neighbourhoods. Age of Empires IV and CS2 overviews never show a town edge this geometric.

The ~700 outcrops and ~900 acacias are invisible in every canonical frame (two lone 'lollipop' trees in S1). S3 is still a uniform beige plane from the camera to a ruler-straight horizon at the plateau rim, with the battery pad as a raised hard-edged beige slab. S6 shows the same straight rim, with the town sitting on a featureless sheet. TW:WH3 and Iron Harvest foregrounds always carry rock, relief or vegetation. Here half the screen is still empty.

Darkening the far facades to 0.25 did not fix S6: the town is still a band of silver-white boxes. The culprit is the window term, not the albedo. Far windows get 2.2x gain (town.js line ~452), and their mix of cool and white temperatures averages, at sub-pixel size, to a cold silver sheen. CS2 skylines at distance read as warm amber specks on dark massing.

Route 31 in S7 and the approach road in S1 are still the darkest, coldest value in the frame: a navy rope that looks raised above the desert. The new 'blend toward desert at distance' is in the town street shader (town.js line 166) and does not seem to reach the regional road ribbons, or it is overridden by fog and specular.

S6's upper two-thirds is near-black with faint vertical blue streaks on the right, which read as banding or ray artefacts rather than sky. In S4, roofs are still flat grey slabs with one box and a red dot, repeated; lots are flat brown; scrub decals are square camo-like tiles with hard edges; and the S3 battery vehicles are box clusters.

env.note: FLAGGED after 4 critic rounds at 5/10 (3 rounds without improvement). Street-level frames (S4/S5) reach ~6–7 and the S7 Moab vista is strong; wide RTS frames still read procedural: octagon town core, trident lanes, invisible rock/acacia scatter (bug: all instances land in one strip), silver far town, navy regional roads. Open issues listed for a follow-up pass.

vfx.name: VFX
vfx.scope: Launches, interceptor trails, intercepts, debris, smoke, screen shake

issues.text: This is unchanged from round 3. C4 f00097: a bright orange J-hook trail curls down the left edge (x~15-30, y~70-240). C4 f00107: it becomes a full-height thin vertical orange line with a pale column beside it, and a broad warm brown-orange wash covers the left 40% of the sky. It reads as a rendering glitch, not a meteor or an impact, and it is in the canonical overhead/street clip.

S6 (t=222.7) still lands between kills, and the frame now shows four round, pale-blue, cotton-ball puffs (about 25-35 px at 1600, x~770-910 y~135-195), each with orange streaks through it. They are the most 'sprite-looking puff / hard-edged circle' element in the shot. C1 f00088 shows the same: tidy round balls beside the star. Broken Arrow's exo-kill remnant is a faint, wide, irregular haze, not a discrete ball. Separately, the short orange dashes around the kills (ballistic hot trails at 25+ km) still read as a fireworks drizzle.

The endo kill aftermath is still an isolated round grey puff, about 40-50 px at 1600 (S5 x~1145 y~370, detached from the burst and its spark spray), and in C4 f00097 a rounded puff sits at x~695 y~140 and another at x~680 y~220. The 12-puff smudge along the path isn't visible as a smear: it is too dim (alpha 0.18) beside the general explosion smoke ball (alpha 0.35-0.5, 12-22 s). CoH3 and WARNO post-kill smoke is torn and directional.

S7 from the high camera: about 8 identical bright starbursts with small pale puffs in an even row along the escarpment (x 770-1310, y 195-250). They read as procedural repetition (identical T_STAR light points, likely ongoing fires and impact flashes). The Nevatim column (x~1000) is modest, about 30 px, and doesn't anchor the frame the way CoH3 aftermath columns do.
In C1 and S6 the Arrow boost trails are still wide, very faint blue vertical bands on the right side of the sky (S6 x 1150-1500). They read as aurora or searchlights, not as missile smoke.
The egg is gone, but the earlier column in C5 (x~488 y~250 at 960) is still a dark, uniform slug that hovers detached from the ground, with no visible fire base or lighter top, beside the hero plume.

audio.name: Audio
audio.scope: Siren timing, spatial audio, impacts, ambience (original/synthesized only)

issues.text: The barrage has no weight. With the trailer camera across the salvo (200-240 s), 17 intercepts and impacts leave short-term loudness flat at about -28 LUFS (LRA 3.6 LU). The biggest event, an impact at 1.8 km, adds only +3.7 dB broadband. Intercepts at 5-8 km add 0 to +2 dB. In the street render (205-232 s), no boom raises the broadband level by more than 0.9 dB under the siren. The loudest thing in the mission is the siren, at -16 LUFS short-term. In CoH3 and WARNO, explosions punch 10-20 LU above the bed. Here the climax plays as a steady siren drone.

Siren level and air filtering are frozen at the listener distance at alert start. E.siren() sets g.gain = distGain(d) and air = airCut(d) once, and the panner has rolloffFactor 0. Panning a 75 s siren from Arad out to Nevatim (7 km), or flying the trailer camera, never changes its loudness or brightness. In the trailer render, the Arad poles stay at a constant -23.5 dB with the d=2.4 km start distance. This fails TARGET §3: 'sources pan and attenuate correctly as the camera moves.' Long launch voices (Arrow 8.5 s) are frozen at the pad position in the same way.

Blast and launch bodies are sine sweeps: crack() adds a sine at 150→42 Hz, and blast() adds a sine at 58→22 Hz. This is the classic 808-kick tell, and every launch and every boom carries the same tonal 'doom' shape. The code comment promises an N-wave, but crack() is a high-passed white-noise spit, not an N-wave.

The tension bed is pure sines: 55, 55.35 and 82.41 Hz, plus static triangle chords at the all-clear. In the post-siren lull (238-246 s), the 55 Hz line alone is -37 dB against a total of -32.6 dB, so a single pure sine carries about 36% of the energy. The 82.8 Hz line adds another -40 dB. It is visible as a constant bright band across every spectrogram. On headphones or a sub, this reads as an electrical hum, not a score.

High-frequency loss with distance is too gentle. airCut() feeds a single 12 dB/oct biquad, and the crack's 'near' term reaches out to 4.4 km. An impact at 2.7 km therefore still prints a crack up to 16 kHz (white line at 209.8 s in the salvo spectrogram), and Sling launches at 1 km show crackle up to 16 kHz. Real air absorption removes nearly everything above about 4 kHz by 2-3 km.

Incoming ballistic missiles make no sound until impact. The recorder skips th.type === 'ballistic' (index.js:145), and nothing synthesizes the re-entry. The tearing roar and sonic-boom double crack of descending re-entry vehicles is the defining sound of the Nevatim strikes. Jets are generic filtered noise, without the ground-reflection comb 'flange' that makes a flyby read as a jet.

The siren contour is a sharp-cornered triangle in log-frequency, because exp ramps produce V-shaped turns at 340 and 708 Hz. The amplitude is perfectly constant, so the short-term level holds flat at about -18.5 LUFS for 25 s in the alert render. Real sirens round off at the turnarounds (motor or driver inertia), and distant poles flutter with wind and turbulence. The constant level also makes the alert beat static for its full ~75 s.

The live siren stop() uses cancelScheduledValues and then setTargetAtTime. If phase 'hold' arrives during the 3.6 s wind-down (likely at 2-4x sim speed, since the siren is scheduled in real time), the exponential ramp is cancelled and the gain jumps back to 1, which pops. Pitch also stays mid-sweep instead of spinning down. At 4x, the siren also outlives its countdown, because cycles are computed in sim seconds but played in real seconds.
Rendered windows start and end mid-waveform: the salvo WAV's first sample is about -19 dBFS (-3573/-2941). A capture muxed from audioOffline() will start with a click.

Every source shares one convolver IR, with fixed discrete slaps at 0.31, 0.57, 1.04 and 1.6 s. Every boom and launch therefore gets the same echo rhythm, independent of where it happened. The cricket loops (7.31 s and 11.07 s) and the 19.7 s wind loop repeat exactly. The wind seam uses a linear crossfade of uncorrelated noise, which dips about 3 dB.

audio.note: Critic R1: 6/10 (judged from spectrograms, measurements and code; nobody has listened). Siren contour, speed-of-sound timing and mix hygiene strong; barrage has no weight, siren level fixed at alert start, 808-style sine bodies, silent re-entries. Round 2 building.

hud.name: HUD & UX
hud.scope: Alert countdown, objectives, shelter routing — cinematic and minimal

issues.text: At the siren (C2 f00040–f00056), the 'WEST LOCKED' and '10 LOCKED OUT' pointers sit in open world space at x≈190–370, not on a screen edge. They are clamped to an inner left bound of 290*mkScale past the roster, or to the projected foot of an 'under' marker. Each pill is the largest element on screen after the alert box, about twice the height of a world chip, and its direction arrow is a 5 px triangle. A player reads them as world labels sitting on random buildings, not as 'over there'. The real Lookout lock and group are visible top-left as a dot plus a '16' chip, so the same trouble shows twice. AoE IV and CoH3 put off-screen alerts flush against the viewport border as small icon tabs, and the minimap carries the ping.

Selecting a group (ux-1, the core routing action) forceFulls every shelter (m.forceFull = !!sel). The town centre becomes a stack of 5–6 long text chips ('LOCKED 260s CLICK: OPEN + SEND', '0/40 248s 32 FREE', '0/28 383s 16 FREE') lifted 24 px above feet that sit close together. Which stem and foot belong to which chip is ambiguous: the 0/40 chip and the 0/28 chip both hover over the same cluster of red diamonds. Unselected groups drop to icon-only dots with no count. CoH3 and AoE IV show a compact cost or ETA tag pinned exactly on the target and keep the long help text in the tooltip or coach line.

In S4b-alert-wide and S2, open shelters are bare icons with no capacity. The brief asks for shelter markers that show capacity, and at the alert a player choosing where to reroute cannot see '0/40' vs '0/12' without zooming or selecting a group. The open shelter icon often sits under its group's chip (S4b: '10 21s' chip over its shelter at 632,378), so the pair reads as one blob. The builder's own gaps (open shelters collapsing to dots mid-zoom, locked S1/S5 as dots at the siren) are confirmed: ux-test reports 'marker dot' for both S1 and S5 when clicked.

The radar now plots shelters and groups, but at 2 px shelter squares and 1.5 px group dots on a 226×118 map where Arad spans a few pixels, the town is an unreadable speck (S2, S4). The locked-shelter ping is the only usable signal. WARNO and Broken Arrow minimaps use clearly sized, shape-coded contacts.

Feed timestamps (10 px, --ink-faint #627580) are still barely legible over bright terrain (S2 bottom right, '23:46'). The feed stacks to the screen edge with no bottom margin matching the command bar. A marker chip pokes out at the left screen edge behind the roster (blue square at x=0 in C2 f00056). Between the siren and the auto-unlock, the Lookout locked shelter in C2 f00040 is a red lock dot jammed between the clock and roster panels.

In S7 (all clear, no town hits) 'No impacts in Arad' still shows '0' with no check while the other three are ticked. The debrief then shows it as done, which is inconsistent. capture.json reports hud update 2.5 ms on the sampled frame against a 4 ms whole-frame JS budget, which is too much for a DOM overlay.

camera.name: Camera & game feel
camera.scope: Intro flyover, input response, hit-stop, alert → shelter → aftermath pacing

issues.oneLine: The trailer's middle (Sling ripple 247-254 s, Nevatim impact 254-257 s) now looks like a Broken Arrow / WARNO air-defence trailer, but the first 5 s and last 10 s carry no action. The intro wadi reads as flying over clouds, and the crest reveals a flat band of lights behind the title, so the stream sits at competent-indie level overall.
strengths: Sling ripple and kills (frames f00048-f00080, sim 248-253.5) are trailer-grade: the battery is anchored low in frame, trails climb through the frame, the kills and burning debris fill the upper half, and the coastline gives depth. It compares well with a Broken Arrow air-defence beat.

The Nevatim impact (f00096-f00108) is shot low and close, with the fireball centred, the inbound trail leading into it and the moon as a counterweight. The impact lands on the beat, like a WARNO close-impact shot.
Shots run at constant velocity through the cuts (keys.linear). A-to-B is effectively one continuous push, and the camera no longer stops at each edit.
The trailer slow-mo now fires deterministically from the script (feelLog: slowmo at simT 250.83, 1.5 s at 0.3x, just after the first Sling kill) and reads as a beat, not lag.

The tactical rig still measures at AoE IV level: tools/input-test.mjs passes 24/24 (1-frame latency, 0% overshoot, 250-270 ms settle, 17.7 m zoom-anchor drift, pitch 35.5 to 31.1 deg, 6 m minimum clearance, clean console).
The siren beat is now readable: C2 at 159.17 vs 160.17 shows a clear push toward the town (expo ease, 1.2 s, under the 1.5 s control cap).
The intro hand-off stays seamless (21.5 to 24 s, same pose with the HUD fading in). The low pass over the towers at 17 s is the intro's best frame.
No console errors in any capture (S1, intro, trailer, C2, C4, input-test).

issues.text: Shot F (262-272 s, a third of the trailer) is a near-static wide view across an empty grey plain: three thin smoke columns 6 km away, the moon dead centre and a few trails at the top edge. The camera moves about 40 m/s at 6.5 km range, so there is no parallax and successive frames look identical (f00126, f00156, f00176). A CoH3 or WARNO trailer would never hold 10 s on this; it reads as the clip running out of material.
issues.fix: src/camera/paths.js TRAILER shot F: cut it to 3-4 s and move the camera to 300-600 m from a Nevatim burn site, low (20-40 m AGL with agl:true), with hangars or wreckage in the foreground and a lateral dolly (about 30 m/s at that range gives real parallax). Or end on a rising pull-back over Arad's rooftops with the smoke drifting across the skyline (subject = the smoke column, anchor = town centre [0,30,0], p moving from 400 to 900 m altitude). Use the freed 6 s to push the opening later (see issue 2).

issues.text: 240-245 s is a slow push over the rooftops toward a horizon with nothing in the sky. Warheads are said to be inbound, but no trail or flash appears until the first Sling launch at about 245 s (f00030). The first 5 s of a trailer are its hook; here they show an empty night town.
issues.fix: Either start the recommended capture later (--t 243.5) and extend shot A's first key to 243.5, or keep 240 and aim shot A's subject at the inbound salvo's logged position at 240-244 (s keyed to the warheads, not the fixed point [-120,140,-1080]) so re-entry streaks are visible above the skyline. Otherwise open on the drone or cruise-missile layer if one is airborne then.

issues.area: intro: wadi climb and crest reveal
issues.text: 0-8 s skims 20 m over a lumpy, uniformly lit surface with a rolled horizon. It reads as flying over a cloud deck, not up a desert wadi: no walls, no rim and no sense of climbing (intro f00010 at t=5). At the crest (9.5-12 s, S1-intro at 11 s) Arad is still a thin band of lights about 3 km off on a featureless plain, sitting directly behind the IRON WALL title. AoE IV and Iron Harvest openers land the reveal on a close, framed subject. Here the reveal only works at 17 s, after the title has gone.
issues.fix: src/camera/paths.js introKeys: route keys 2.6-8.2 along the actual escarpment face (sample groundAt to find where the slope is steepest and fly beside it, so the cliff fills one third of the frame), and look up-slope rather than along the ground so the rim reads as a skyline edge. Pull the crest key (9.2) 1-1.5 km closer to Arad and drop it to 25-35 m above a ridge, so the town rises above a dark foreground line. Bring the 15.6-18 s low tower pass forward to 11-14 s so the title lands on the strongest frame. Ask HUD to raise the title into the upper sky band, or delay it by about 1 s.

issues.area: trailer: Arrow and Sling-kill shots lose the town
issues.text: Shots C (250-254) and E (257.6-262) put the camera 3+ km from Arad, so the town is a 3% sliver of lights on the bottom edge. In E the Arrow 3 star-flashes hang in empty sky over a bare plain, with the only ground interest a Nevatim smoke column at the right edge (f00126). Without the defended town under the flashes the stakes vanish, unlike Broken Arrow's interceptions over a skyline.
issues.fix: paths.js TRAILER C/E: place the camera inside or at the edge of Arad (e.g. p ~[-300, 60-90, 200] with agl:true), looking east and up past the nearest towers, so rooftops fill the lower 25-30% and the flashes sit in the upper third. frameLook already allows this: keep a: [0,30,0] but bring p within 400-800 m of it and raise fov to 64-68 so a 60-70 deg elevation spread still fits.

issues.area: trailer feel: hit-stop overuse at distance
issues.text: In the trailer the hit-stop distance gate is bypassed (index.js: `|| scriptName === 'trailer'`), so six 55 ms hit-stops fire on kills 8.4-39 km from the camera, and a second slow-mo (Arrow, 258.82) follows 8 s after the Sling one. A freeze for a pinpoint flash 39 km away reads as a dropped frame in the exported video, not impact (TARGET §5: hit-stop must never feel like lag). Two slow-mos in 30 s also dilute the first.
issues.fix: src/camera/index.js intercept handler: in trailer mode keep the onScreen && d < 9000 gate (or script hit-stops explicitly like slingSlow), and skip the auto Arrow slow-mo when a scripted slow-mo has fired in the last 15 s (set slowDone = true inside script()).

issues.area: trailer: Nevatim reads as a sea
issues.text: In shot D the camera is so low over the flat, sheen-lit plain that the base ground reads like water, and Nevatim shows as scattered dark boxes with no hangar or shelter silhouette near the camera. The impact is strong, but its setting is anonymous.
issues.fix: paths.js shot D: raise it to 90-120 m AGL and pick p so that a hardened shelter or the runway edge sits in the near foreground between the camera and the impact (look up Nevatim structure positions in src/world), and pitch down slightly so the runway lines give perspective.

issues.benchmarkNotes: AoE IV (camera feel): the tactical rig matches it on every measured axis (input-test 24/24) and would pass alone. AoE IV / Iron Harvest (intro): the structure and hand-off are right, but the 0-8 s wadi has no walls and reads as a cloud deck, and the crest reveal is a distant band behind the title. The good frames come at 15-18 s after the title has gone. Roughly 5-6. Broken Arrow / WARNO (trailer): 247-257 s is at or near the bar (Sling ripple with kills and debris, close Nevatim impact with slow-mo punctuation), a big step up. But 240-245 has no action, 262-272 is 10 s of near-static distant smoke on an empty plain, and the Arrow shot loses the town. Half the 30 s would be cut from a real trailer: roughly 6. CoH3 (pacing beats): the siren push is now readable and stays within the control cap. Weighted toward the trailer as the final deliverable, the stream scores 6.
